Internal helper: a column's lettered missing-value markers made plain NA

Source: R/io.R
dot-jst_zap_tags.Rd

haven::zap_missing() turns a labelled column's Stata-style and SAS-style markers into plain NA and drops the labels attached to them, but its method for a plain double returns the column unchanged – and a Stata file whose extended missing values carry no value label loads as exactly that, a double holding tagged NAs. Until Session 372 the two callers passed such a column through with its markers in place: jsave(preserve.declarations = FALSE) then repeated the .sav and .xpt refusal that had offered it, and jload(preserve.declarations = FALSE) and jconvert(to = "baseR") reported as plain NA markers that were still there. Here every marker cell becomes plain NA, labelled or not. Callers: .jst_handle_udms() and jconvert()'s base R arm. The analysis pipeline's mask (.jst_apply_declared_udms_as_na()) keeps haven::zap_missing(): a plain double's tagged cells are NA to every count, and with no labels there is nothing for as_factor() to revive, so a zap there would change nothing.

Usage

.jst_zap_tags(col)

Arguments

col

A column.

Value

The column with its markers plain NA. A column that is not a double holds none and is returned unchanged.
